newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FINLAND "VERY SATISFIED" WITH ERM RATE - AKERHOLM.
newsitem.headline: FINLAND "VERY SATISFIED" WITH ERM RATE - AKERHOLM.

text.p: Finland is very pleased with its entry rate into the European Union's exchange rate mechanism, finance ministry under-secretary of state Johnny Akerholm said.

Akerholm, speaking to reporters in Brussels after the EU monetary committee on Saturday agreed to bring in Finland into the currency grid at a central rate of 3.04 to the German mark, also said the move would not affect Finnish exports.
"We are very satisifed with the rate," he said.

Asked whether it was a devaluation as the central rate was weaker than the level at which the markka traded on Friday, he said: "No, certainly not...the market rate for Friday was just one point in a long-term development."
Akerholm said the link would increase Finland's chances of meeting all the single currency criteria.
"It doesn't mean any real change for Finnish exports or for the Finnish economy as such," he said.
Bank of Finland director Matti Vanhala said the link could have a stabilising effect on the exchange rate.
"The EMU commitment is firmer, at least in the eyes of markets and that could have a stabilising effect on exchange rates," he told reporters.
